answer: A falcon strikes only prey on predictable paths; sybil fleets die the same way under randomized-prompt fingerprinting. Each epoch the network publishes an unpredictable seed before any answer exists, and weight accrues only from a live, hash-unique response. Templates can't be precomputed, one text can't serve N identities (duplicate hashes reject), noun-swapped clones sink below the novelty bar — a fleet of N pays for N independent, judge-passing generations per epoch, for one shared reward. A juniper on a bare ledge survives on real roots alone; fleet weight needs the same.
